units.source_text: 這幾個字倏地一下掠過我大腦的一隅，使我猛然一驚。

en.t: Those few words flashed across one corner of my mind, making me start in surprise.

units.source_text: 說不準陀思妥耶夫斯基不會把罪惡當作同義詞，而是把這兩個字刻意排列在一起呢。

en.t: Perhaps Dostoevsky had not treated crime and punishment as synonyms, but had deliberately placed those two words side by side.

units.source_text: 罪與罰，絕無相通之處，而是水火不容的兩個字。

en.t: Crime and punishment had nothing in common at all; they were two words as incompatible as fire and water.

units.source_text: 把罪與罰視為反詞的陀思妥耶夫斯基，他筆下的綠藻、惡臭的水池、亂麻交錯的內心……

en.t: Dostoevsky, who saw crime and punishment as opposites, and the green scum, fetid pools, and tangled inner depths in his writing...
Ah, I understand it now. No, not yet...

units.source_text: 正當這些思考如走馬燈一樣，不斷在我的腦際閃現著旋轉時，

en.t: Just as these thoughts kept flashing and spinning through my mind like a revolving lantern,

units.source_text: 堀木喊道：「喂！這哪是什麼蠶豆啊，你快過來！」

en.t: Horiki shouted, "Hey! This is no broad bean. Come here!"

units.source_text: 堀木的聲音和表情驟變。

en.t: Horiki's voice and expression changed abruptly.
